headline: High risk of data leakage and capability conflict: nullclaw’s broad workspace/network access can feed sensitive outputs into transformers pipelines by default.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: nullclaw can read/write a shared workspace and use MCP, while transformers can ingest files and stdin/stdout as pipeline inputs. That creates a plausible instruction-injection path if nullclaw writes attacker-controlled content that transformers later parses. The pair lacks documented provenance or isolation, so I choose medium rather than low.
conditions: IF nullclaw writes untrusted text into a file that transformers later consumes as prompts or instructions
IF transformers is run on content from nullclaw without provenance filtering
mitigations: Separate the agents into distinct directories
Add a manual review step before transformers consumes nullclaw-generated files
Disable MCP paths that can write prompt-like artifacts
Use allowlisted input filenames only
requires-engineering: add provenance tags to all handoffs

B_data_leakage.rationale: nullclaw explicitly touches API keys, private keys, bearer tokens, and conversation history, and it has broad network egress plus filesystem access. transformers also has broad egress and can process files and model inputs. In default shared-workspace use, sensitive material from nullclaw can flow into transformers outputs or outbound requests, creating a realistic exfiltration path.
conditions: IF both agents share a workspace containing secrets or conversation history
IF transformers is invoked on files produced by nullclaw that contain sensitive data
mitigations: Move secrets to a separate vault path
Run transformers on redacted copies only
Restrict outbound network for one agent during handoff
Review shared workspace permissions
requires-engineering: enforce per-agent data-loss-prevention filters

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Both agents have filesystem write and broad network egress, and nullclaw also modifies git state. If they operate on the same directory or repository, concurrent writes and git mutations can overwrite each other or corrupt state. No locking or coordination primitive is documented for the pair, so the overlap is dangerous by default.
conditions: IF both agents are pointed at the same working tree
IF nullclaw and transformers run concurrently without external locking
mitigations: Assign separate working directories
Serialize git operations manually
Pause one agent before the other writes
Use branch-per-agent workflows
requires-engineering: add file locks or transactional workspace coordination

D_cascading_error.rationale: nullclaw can produce webhook payloads, agent-card metadata, and other outputs that transformers may treat as input for downstream processing. transformers is a document-processing pipeline, so it may render or transform those outputs without strong verification. The pathway exists in default workflows, but the blast radius is usually bounded to incorrect documents or derived artifacts.
conditions: IF transformers consumes nullclaw-generated text as authoritative input
IF downstream actions are taken from transformed output without human review
mitigations: Require human approval before downstream use
Insert a verification step between agents
Mark nullclaw outputs as untrusted by default
Limit transformers to formatting-only tasks
requires-engineering: add schema validation for handoff payloads

E_compliance.rationale: nullclaw explicitly handles secrets, audit logs, and conversation history, while transformers processes multimodal data with no stated retention or residency controls. Because the pair lacks documented compliance alignment, sensitive data could be retained or processed under mismatched policies. I cite both profiles because the risk arises from their combined handling of regulated data classes.
conditions: IF regulated data such as conversation history or secrets is routed through both agents
IF retention or residency requirements apply to the shared workflow
mitigations: Avoid sending regulated data through the pair
Document retention expectations for both agents
Purge shared workspaces after each run
Restrict logs to non-sensitive metadata
requires-engineering: align compliance controls and data-processing agreements
